questions_and_answers.question: Compound interest is usually better than simple interest because it pays interest on the principal and the interest earned in each period. interest on the entire principal rather than the interest in each period. more, as it is matched by an employer's 401k contribution. more often throughout the year rather than once a year.
questions_and_answers.answer: interest on the principal and the interest earned in each period.. Compound interest is better than simple interest because it pays interest on the principal and the interest earned in each period. This means that the interest earned in each period is added to the principal, and then the interest is calculated on the new, larger principal in the next period. This leads to exponential growth of the investment over time. Simple interest, on the other hand, only pays interest on the original principal amount. This means that the interest earned each period is not added to the principal, and the interest earned in each period is always the same. The other options are incorrect. Compound interest is not matched by an employer's 401k contribution, and it is not necessarily paid more often throughout the year than simple interest.
